text: Build job 5, part 2, of the records-history plan (docs/design/records-history.md section 4 and 10, decision D111): the legacy rule. For main's commits up to and including a cutover commit C0, the attribution check delegates to the existing history-check logic (athena-gate) unchanged, except that the exempt list is read from a legacy-exempt record on athena/records (the record type exists in athena-data history.rs) instead of athena.toml's [history] exempt; commits after C0 keep the records-only rule from part 1. Add a way to produce that legacy-exempt record from athena.toml's current list and comments (the six entries plus 02837e0, each with its reason), without writing it to the real branch yet. Tests: each of the seven named commits (49c6ac1, 64ecdc9, ee4b0dd, f2a8453, 5a73478, 39962ed, 02837e0) is judged as section 4 says when its legacy-exempt entry is present, and fails as today when it is absent; a legacy-exempt record that later gains an entry is refused (append-only). C0 is a parameter; nothing chooses it yet.
